speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You are here with postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness; how long has it been since your delivery, and exactly when did the fever start?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your prolonged labor and 11-pound baby, we need to rule out complications like uterine atony or infection; did you have an episiotomy or any tearing during delivery? Also, what does your fever look like in terms of temperature and duration? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and CRP.

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results showing "normal readings" are ambiguous; could you clarify specifically which tests were performed and confirm if your white blood cell count, C-reactive protein, and urinalysis were all within normal limits? Additionally, given the 11-pound baby and decreased bowel sounds, do you have any history of obstetric fistula or pelvic inflammatory disease prior to this pregnancy?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Urachal Abscess (presenting as postpartum fever, suprapubic tenderness, urinary frequency, and ileus due to decreased bowel sounds).
